### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A21, A22, A23 and A24 each appear in about 28% of traces, down from about 83% (e.g., A21 from 83% to 28%, A22 from 82.5% to 28.5%). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- Activities A25, A26, A27 and A28 each appear in about 73% of traces, up from about 18% (e.g., A25 from 18.5% to 73%, A26 from 18% to 73.5%). [OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011]
- A04 appears in about 16% of traces, down from about 55%. [OCC002]
- The successor of A20 changed: before, about 83% of its outgoing transitions went to A24 and 17% to A28; after, about 72% go to A28 and 27% to A24. [DIR003]
- The successor of A31 changed: before, about 53% went to A04 and 45% to A19; after, about 84% go to A19 and 5% to A04. [DIR004]
- Co-occurrence patterns shifted accordingly: A04 co-occurs with A19 in about 16% of traces instead of 55%; A19 co-occurs with A21–A24 in about 28% instead of 83%, and with A25–A28 in about 73% instead of 18%. [REL001, REL013, REL017]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process changed such that a set of activities (A21–A24, and A04) was largely replaced by another set (A25–A28, and A02/A08) in the later window. This is directly shown by the drop in participation of the former and rise of the latter, and by the routing changes: A20 now leads to A28 instead of A24, and A31 now leads to A19 instead of A04. The co-occurrence and lag patterns are consistent with this swap. A competing explanation that the later window simply contains more cases of an alternative branch cannot be ruled out, but that would still be a structural change in routing shares. The evidence does not indicate why the change occurred.
